name: Costa Rica
dek: Juan Santamaría International Airport, WMO 78762, in the Central Valley.
paragraphs: The reference station is Juan Santamaría International Airport, WMO 78762, height 913 m. The Costa Rican submission also has Tobías Bolaños, Daniel Oduber (Liberia), and Puerto Limón; none were averaged in. The precipitation row counts 29 years. The highs were checked against the Instituto Meteorológico Nacional's own airport climatology and agree within about half a degree. No official driving-side source for Costa Rica was found on this pass.

The highest average high in the table is 33.1 °C, in April. The lowest average low is 15.0 °C, in January and February. The wettest month by the precipitation column is September, at 320.0 mm, and the driest is January, at 7.9 mm.

climate.caption: Reference station: Juan Santamaría International Airport, WMO 78762. Not the coasts.
climate.note: World Meteorological Organization 1991–2020 climatological standard normals, distributed by NOAA NCEI. Monthly values are copied as printed, with leading spaces removed; a value printed with no leading zero, such as -.3, is shown as -0.3. The file prints the position to the minute only, 09°59′N and 084°10′W. Its precipitation number-of-years row reads 29. The highs were checked against the Instituto Meteorológico Nacional's aeronautical climatology for the airport (2010–2025 daily data), whose average maximums run 29.9–33.1 °C, also peaking at 33.1 °C in April; that table covers a different period and was not mixed in.
climate.sourceTitle: WMO climate normals 1991-2020, Juan Santamaría International Airport (78762)

plugs.detail: The IEC world-plugs list, in the copy archived on 16 August 2026, shows Costa Rica at the voltage, frequency, and plug types in the figure. A direct download of the live page did not return the list, so the archive is the copy that was read.

tipping.label: Tipping
tipping.detail: Visit Costa Rica says that in restaurants and hotels the 13% value added tax and a 10% tip are included in the final price, and that you are welcome to leave an additional gratuity if you are exceptionally happy with the service.

water.label: Tap water
water.detail: CDC's traveler page for Costa Rica, last reviewed September 18, 2026, does not say whether tap water is safe or unsafe. It says food and water standards around the world vary based on the destination, that standards may also differ within a country, and that risk may change depending on the activity. It points readers to CDC's food and water precautions. This page does not turn that into medical advice.

currency.label: Currency
currency.detail: ISO 4217 lists the currency name Costa Rican Colon and the code CRC for Costa Rica.

timeZone.label: Time zone
timeZone.detail: IANA's zone.tab and zone1970.tab each give Costa Rica one row, America/Costa_Rica. There is no second zone for the country in either file.

entry.label: Official entry requirements
entry.note: The tourism board's entry requirements page. The immigration service's site refused an automated request on 15 November 2026. We do not restate a visa rule.

bestTime.intro: Month by month, from the San José airport table above and the Costa Rica Tourism Board's climate page, which describes two regimes. The Pacific side has a well-defined dry and a rainy season: the dry season runs December to March, April is a transition, the rainy season runs May to October and November is a transition. The Caribbean side has no well-defined dry season: rain stays between 100 and 200 mm in its driest months, with relatively dry spells in February–March and September–October. The airport is in the Central Valley at 913 m; it is neither coast.

months.note: Pacific dry season. Airport average high 30.7 °C, low 15.0 °C, 7.9 mm, the driest month in the table. Caribbean side: inside its strongest rainy period, November to January.
Pacific dry season. Airport 32.0 °C / 15.0 °C, 10.4 mm. Caribbean side: one of its two relatively dry periods (February–March).
Pacific dry season. Airport 32.9 °C / 15.6 °C, 17.3 mm. The tourism board calls March the driest and hottest month on the Pacific side; at the airport station, April's average high is 0.2 °C higher.
Pacific transition month. Airport 33.1 °C / 16.2 °C, 80.6 mm, the highest average high in the table.
Pacific rainy season begins. Airport 31.9 °C / 16.7 °C, 261.9 mm. Caribbean side: its second rainy period runs May to August.

Pacific rainy season, with the relative lull the tourism board calls veranillo, or "little summer," in July and August. Airport 31.1 °C / 16.7 °C, 167.2 mm, lower than June or August. Caribbean side: the page puts a rain maximum in July.
Pacific rainy season, still in the veranillo. Airport 31.2 °C / 16.5 °C, 224.3 mm.

Pacific rainy season; the tourism board names September and October the rainiest months there. Airport 31.1 °C / 16.3 °C, 320.0 mm, the wettest month in the table. Caribbean side: one of its relatively dry periods (September–October).
Pacific rainy season. Airport 30.5 °C / 16.2 °C, 317.0 mm. Caribbean side: still in its relatively dry spell.
Pacific transition month. Airport 30.3 °C / 15.5 °C, 165.8 mm. Caribbean side: its strongest rainy period begins (November to January).
Pacific dry season begins. Airport 30.6 °C / 15.4 °C, 31.0 mm. Caribbean side: the tourism board says December is its rainiest month.
